Hero.desc1: Your neighbour in Ward 22 — at your doors, on your streets, and listening first. Running for Ottawa City Council to make sure residents have a strong voice at City Hall.
Hero.desc2: Ward 22 deserves a councillor who is present, practical and accountable — and committed to making sure residents have a strong voice at City Hall.
Hero.eyebrow: Candidate for Ward 22 Riverside South and Findlay Creek
Hero.positioning: Not politics first. People first. I don't have all the answers. I listen first. I identify the problem. I work with residents. I find practical solutions. And I hold City Hall accountable for delivering them.

Mission.m1_desc: A ward where residents feel safe walking, cycling, and driving.
Mission.m2_desc: Transit that is frequent, reliable, and worth leaving the car at home for.
Mission.m3_desc: Programs that prepare the next generation for a rapidly changing world.
Mission.m4_desc: Services and facilities that keep pace with Ward 22's rapid growth.
Mission.m5_desc: A councillor who listens first and advocates for residents at City Hall.
Mission.banner1: The vision for Ward 22 is simple: a ward where every family can live safely, move freely, raise their children with opportunity, and access the services and spaces they deserve.

Priorities.desc: Built from thousands of conversations with residents across Riverside South and Findlay Creek.
Priorities.p1_desc: Make Ward 22 safer for families, pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers by addressing speeding, improving road safety, enhancing street lighting, and investing in safer parks, pathways, and public spaces.
p1_bullets: Safer routes for children and seniors
Priorities.p1_quote: Every resident deserves to feel safe in their neighbourhood, whether walking to school, cycling to a park, or driving home.
Priorities.p2_desc: Give young people practical opportunities to build the future — through STEM and AI, arts and creativity, entrepreneurship, leadership, mentorship, skilled trades, and summer opportunities, in partnership with schools, businesses and community organizations.
Priorities.p2_quote: Youth should not just be prepared for the future — they should be given opportunities to build it.
Priorities.p3_desc: Advocate for reliable transit service and practical traffic solutions that reduce congestion, improve connectivity, and address the everyday transportation challenges residents face.
Priorities.p3_quote: Residents should spend less time stuck in traffic and more time with their families.
Priorities.p4_title: Infrastructure That Keeps Pace With Growth
Priorities.p4_desc: Ward 22 is growing quickly. City services and infrastructure need to grow with it — from parks and recreation to walking and cycling connections, everyday services, and stronger advocacy at City Hall.
p4_bullets: Stronger advocacy at City Hall for growth-related infrastructure
Priorities.p4_quote: Growth must be matched by the infrastructure and services residents need to thrive.
Priorities.p1_action: What This Means: I will work with City staff and Ottawa Police to implement traffic calming in high-risk areas, advocate for better lighting in our parks, and ensure crosswalks are safer for our children and seniors.
Priorities.p2_action: What This Means: I will champion a Ward 22 Youth Advisory Council, establish partnerships with local businesses for mentorship and summer jobs, and advocate for community spaces that support STEM, arts, and leadership programs.
Priorities.p3_action: What This Means: I will advocate for better OC Transpo reliability, push for solutions to traffic bottlenecks in our neighbourhoods, and ensure residents have practical commuting options.
Priorities.p4_action: What This Means: I will demand that our ward gets its fair share of infrastructure funding, prioritize new parks and recreational facilities, and advocate for infrastructure and essential service to keep pace with our communities growth.

Community.title: Built from thousands of conversations on your streets.
Community.desc: Ward 22 is one of Ottawa's fastest-growing communities. Over the next four years, the ward will add thousands of new residents, new families, and new demands on infrastructure, services, and community spaces.
Community.c1_desc: 5,000+ doors reached since June 2026 across Riverside South and Findlay Creek — listening before forming any platform commitments.
Community.c2_desc: Served on the Board of the Findlay Creek Community Association, contributing to community advocacy and local engagement.
Community.c3_desc: Experience serving on a local political association board, with a focus on organization, engagement and community outreach.
Community.c4_desc: Distributed 5,000 door hangers with a community survey to gather resident feedback that helped inform campaign priorities.
Community.c5_desc: Welcoming Ward 22 residents who want to help build a stronger community.
Community.c6_desc: Active on Facebook and Instagram — connecting with Ward 22 residents daily across Riverside South and Findlay Creek.

About.eyebrow: Candidate for Ward 22 Riverside South and Findlay Creek
About.p1: As a finance professional with an Executive MBA from the Ivey Business School, I understand the importance of responsible planning, informed decision-making and delivering results. But I also know that numbers and spreadsheets never tell the whole story. The people who live here do. That is why I have spent time listening directly to residents across Riverside South and Findlay Creek.
About.p2: Canada gave our family opportunity. Ward 22 gave us home. I am running because I want to help make sure this community continues to grow in a way that works for the families who call it home.
About.quote_home: "Canada gave our family opportunity. Ward 22 gave us home."
About.trait1: Finance professional — corporate planning and resource allocation
About.trait2: Executive MBA — Ivey Business School, Western University
About.trait3: Career focused on long-term planning and responsible decision-making
About.quote_page: "Canada gave our family opportunity. Ward 22 gave us home."

Running.title: Why I'm Running
Running.subtitle: This wasn't a decision made at a desk. It came from living here.
Running.name: Muyiwa Ojo
Running.p1: I am Muyiwa Ojo — a husband, father of two, and proud Ward 22 resident who calls this community home with my wife and our two children.
Running.p2: Like many of you, we chose Ward 22 because of what it promised: safe streets, strong schools, and a place where families could put down roots and thrive. In many ways, it has delivered on that promise.
Running.p3: Over the years, I have also seen where we can do better.
Running.p4: As our community grows, young families need more parks, programs, and spaces where children can learn, play, and thrive. Residents spend too much time commuting when better transit connections could make the journey shorter and less stressful. And our ward is expanding faster than some of the infrastructure and services needed to support it.
Running.p5: Professionally, I work in finance and hold an Executive MBA from the Ivey Business School. My career has taught me the importance of planning for growth, making responsible decisions, and ensuring resources are used effectively. To me, good governance is built on those same principles: listening to people, setting priorities, and delivering results that improve everyday life.
Running.p6: But my decision to run wasn’t made in a boardroom or classroom. It came from living here.
Running.p7: It came from conversations with neighbours. From seeing families navigate crowded parks and growing communities. From hearing residents talk about traffic, housing, local services, and the future they want for Ward 22.
Running.p8: Those conversations led me to file my nomination on May 1, 2026.
Running.p9: I am not running because I have all the answers. I am running because I believe the best solutions come from the people who live here. My role is to listen, bring people together, and ensure residents have a strong voice at City Hall.
Running.p10: Since filing my nomination, I have spent my time where it matters most — at your doors, on your streets, and in your neighbourhoods, listening to your concerns, ideas, and aspirations for our community.
Running.p11: I am not a career politician. I am a neighbour who cares deeply about Ward 22 and its future.
Running.quote: I am not running because I have all the answers. I am running because I believe the best solutions come from the people who live here.
Running.p12: Ward 22 deserves a councillor who is present, practical, accountable, and committed to serving every resident.
Running.p13: This community is our home. Together, we can build a Ward 22 that keeps pace with growth, protects what makes our neighbourhood special, and creates real opportunities for every family who calls it home.

Testimonials.title: Voices from Across the Ward.
Testimonials.quote1: Muyiwa shows up, listens, and follows through. That's exactly what Ward 22 needs at the council table.
Testimonials.quote2: He's focused on the practical things — the services, the streets, the everyday issues that too often get ignored.
Testimonials.quote3: A steady, thoughtful voice. Muyiwa understands that good government is in the details.

We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to any third party.

Fonts are self-hosted and do not make any external CDN requests. The ward survey links to a <googleLink>Google Forms</googleLink> page hosted by Google; by following that link you are subject to <googleLink>Google's Privacy Policy</googleLink> — no data is shared with us automatically by Google. Stripe may collect payment information in accordance with their own <stripeLink>Privacy Policy</stripeLink>. We do not store full credit card details on our servers. All payment data is handled in accordance with PCI-DSS standards. Donation records may be subject to disclosure requirements under Ontario municipal election finance rules.
Privacy.section4_body: This website may use essential cookies to operate correctly. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies. No personal data is collected through cookies.
Privacy.section5_body: We retain personal information for the duration of the 2026 election campaign and as required by Ontario election finance regulations. After this period, information will be securely deleted.
